title: They eat, to forget, what's your name?
summary: For -er verbs, ils mangent sounds exactly like il mange. The written -ent is silent. With verbs starting with a vowel you hear the liaison: il oublie vs ils oublient ('il-zoublie'). Outside verbs, -ent sounds like 'an': différent, appartement. Comment tu t'appelles ? = What's your name? Je m'appelle… = My name is…
points: je mange / tu manges / il mange / ils mangent all sound the same. Context tells you who.
With vowel-initial verbs, liaison shows the plural: elle oublie / elles oublient ('el-zoublie').
-ent at the end of a non-verb sounds like 'an': différent, un appartement.
appeler = to call. The e changes in j'appelle / tu t'appelles.
Comment tu t'appelles ? = What's your name? (literally 'how do you call yourself?')
drills: They fish in order to eat.
I want to find an apartment.
